clue.text: Concert work bringing in tango in timely fashion

indicators.note: bringing something in takes it inside, so one piece is lodged within another

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
to ply is to work steadily at a trade
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A concert piece that brings in a tango, played right on cue.
explanation.walkthrough: The tango slips into the second word, after its first letter, and the concert stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Promptly is an adverb meaning without delay, at the right moment, so it swaps for the phrase about timeliness.

clue.text: Priest brought in Roman Catholic memento

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so the priest goes within the church letters

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A priest has been handed a Catholic keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object kept from the past as a reminder, a keepsake or souvenir.

clue.text: Satisfied about blokes and love? It's a thing of the past

indicators.note: one word placed about another wraps around it

blocks.note: to have met a demand is to have satisfied it
blokes are men
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Content with men and romance? Looks like nostalgia talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake that reminds you of an earlier time, an object belonging to the past.

clue.text: British soldier dismissing Military Medal as trifle

indicators.note: dismissing sends something away, so those letters are taken out of the soldier

blocks.note: Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the nickname for a British private soldier
MM is the abbreviation for the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A British soldier stripped of his medal is treated as of little account.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the medal's two letters from the soldier's nickname leaves TO and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy can be a trifle, a thing of little value; both also work as verbs for idly playing with something.

clue.text: Certainly ready to change after time in the recent past

indicators.note: letters told to change move into a new order

blocks.note: yes, certainly
T is the abbreviation for time
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to change once the moment comes, as they were only lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After time' places the rearranged letters behind the T, with the affirmative word at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday as an adverb means on the previous day, or loosely in times just gone by, which is the recent past.

clue.text: Mike joining excellent club

blocks.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A man called Mike signs up to a top-notch club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society to join; it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked or flanged head, used as a weapon.

clue.text: Doctor taking tea and coffee

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: The doctor has a cup of tea and a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' here only joins the two parts side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee originally shipped from the Yemeni port of Mocha, or a chocolate-flavoured coffee drink.

clue.text: Trumpet family's taken around carnival city

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family

explanation.surface: A family holiday with a trumpeter in tow around Rio's carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: The family wraps the city, which sits between its A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion is a medieval shrill trumpet, the source of the phrase clarion call.

clue.text: Hurry to protect one manuscript likely to fall apart

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround and shield it

blocks.note: to fly is to rush or hurry
the Roman numeral for one
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: Rush to save a single fragile old manuscript before it crumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimsy means weak and insubstantial, so a flimsy thing is liable to break up.

clue.text: Very good spies start to like being gregarious

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, the definition the adjective 'gregarious'

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: so means very, as in 'so good'; the pair stand for the one small intensifier
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Top spies who start to warm to someone turn out to be quite outgoing.
explanation.walkthrough: The opener is a loose way to give SO: 'very' does the work, with 'good' as part of the phrase being intensified.
explanation.definitionFit: Social and gregarious both describe someone who enjoys company and mixing with other people.

clue.text: Religious image I study

blocks.note: taken as written
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: I am studying a holy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a devotional painting of a holy figure, especially in the Orthodox Church.

clue.text: Change in climate's doing for flower

blocks.note: all eight letters, the S included, rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Change in climate' reads as global warming; 'doing for' (finishing off) is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant grown for its large showy blooms, so it counts as a flower.

clue.text: Military figure, computer expert, embracing married bloke

explanation.definitionFit: A commander is an officer in charge of a force, and a naval rank, so a military figure.

explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the months behind the shortened report.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm can mean an outburst or uproar, as in a storm of protest, which is a commotion.

clue.text: One studying sun's capturing carbon and hydrogen

blocks.note: solar means of the sun

H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a student holding a scholarship, someone engaged in study.

clue.text: Sewer noise requiring intervention of soldiers

blocks.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe or channel carrying away waste water, which is what a sewer does.

clue.text: Difficult Republican couple trapped in Australia

indicators.note: something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: AUS is the abbreviation for Australia

clue.text: Moving quickly to contain injury, getting source of medical advice

clue.text: Nonsense about very large perch

clue.text: US city series to make you beam

taken as written
the opening letter of the word

the first letter of the word
